observations.statement: Ordinary Schengen visa coverage does not itself extend to Greenland; distinguish visa territorial validity from a guaranteed admission decision.
Qualifying residence permits/cards can exempt the traveller; a D visa from another Schengen state is not the same document.
Bangladesh is listed as visa-required for Denmark; this provides a nationality candidate, not a complete traveller-class audit.
Overseas-specific visa coverage and exemptions must be assessed together; residence, D visas and certain French multiple-entry visas prevent a blanket C-visa claim.
FCDO reports a permit and organised-tour requirement and possible abrupt restrictions; this is foreign advice, not a local legal proof.
NIA describes permits for non-open areas and a conditional no-further-approval statement for group itineraries without those areas.
The read sources do not establish identity between the TAR tourism permit and the general NIA travel permit; combining their attributes would be unsupported.
